title: Aperol Spritz
intro: The Venetian 3-2-1 rule: prosecco, Aperol and a splash of soda.

steps.t: Fill a large wine glass with ice.
Pour in the chilled prosecco.
Add the Aperol, then the soda.
Stir gently once and garnish with half an orange slice.

tips.t: Pour the prosecco before the Aperol so it doesn't sink to the bottom.
Use Campari instead of Aperol for a more bitter, Venetian-style spritz.
Serve with olives, crisps and little sandwiches.

title: Americano
intro: Campari and sweet vermouth lengthened with soda: bitter, light and very Milanese.

steps.t: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Pour in the Campari and sweet vermouth.
Top with the soda and stir briefly with a bar spoon.
Garnish with half an orange slice and the lemon peel twisted over the top.

tips.t: Replace the soda with 30 ml gin and you have a Negroni.
Serve with taralli, salted peanuts or crostini.

title: Hugo
intro: Prosecco, elderflower syrup, mint and lime: South Tyrol's floral aperitivo.

steps.t: Put the mint in a large wine glass and press it lightly with a spoon to release its scent.
Add the elderflower syrup, lime slices and ice.
Pour in the prosecco and top with soda.
Stir gently from the bottom up and serve right away.

tips.t: Swap the prosecco for sparkling apple juice to make it alcohol-free.

title: Bellini
intro: White peach purée and prosecco, as at Harry's Bar in Venice.

steps.t: Blend the peach flesh with the lemon juice to a smooth purée.
Push it through a sieve and chill it for 15 minutes along with the flute.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Pour 50 ml purée into the chilled flute.
Add the prosecco slowly with the glass tilted, then stir gently.

tips.t: Purée and prosecco must be ice-cold, or it will foam over.
Strawberry purée instead of peach makes it a Rossini.

title: Rossini
intro: Ripe strawberries puréed with prosecco: the Bellini's springtime sibling.

steps.t: Rinse and hull the strawberries and blend them with the sugar and lemon juice.
Strain the purée through a fine sieve to remove the seeds.
Chill the purée and the flute for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Pour the purée into the flute, add the prosecco slowly and stir gently.

tips.t: Use ripe in-season strawberries; out of season the purée is pale and sour.
White peach instead of strawberries makes it a Bellini.

title: Negroni Sbagliato
intro: Born at Milan's Bar Basso: a Negroni with prosecco in place of the gin.

steps.t: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Pour in the Campari and sweet vermouth and stir for a few seconds.
Top with the cold prosecco, pouring slowly.
Stir once from the bottom and garnish with half an orange slice.

tips.t: Use gin instead of prosecco and you're back to a classic Negroni.
Goes well with mini pizzas, stuffed fried olives or cured meats.
